summary: Binary-verified NOEMA Discovery artifact contained 105 unreviewed candidates and a 30-item priority queue: 6 RECENT_PUBLICATION, 2 UPCOMING_OR_AHEAD_OF_PRINT and 22 NEWLY_INDEXED_LEGACY. Fresh scholarly/public screening added five deduplicated candidate-only records: Late Pleistocene habitual betel-nut use in Sulawesi; two complementary Bianfu Cave Denisovan Nature papers; a modern autism/schizotypy-religiosity study; and a structured historical corpus of more than 2,000 texts on ghost belief and secular critique in early twentieth-century China. One candidate chronology revision was created for psychoactive-plant use. No descent/diffusion relationships, evidence promotions, hypothesis promotions or confidence changes were made.
research_note: Highest-priority human review: Sulawesi betel-nut chronology and the Bianfu Denisovan pair. Preserve strict separation between psychoactive exposure and ritual meaning; molecular taxonomic attribution and artifact authorship; modern neurocognitive trait associations and retrospective diagnosis; and public historical rhetoric versus private belief or population prevalence.
